title: Merchant Dispute Resolution Portal
objectives: Reduce average dispute handling time from 11 days to 4 days.
Reduce disputes lost due to missed deadlines from 18% to under 5%.
Cut operations analyst effort per dispute by 40%.
in_scope: Integration with the card network dispute APIs (Visa and Mastercard) and the internal payments ledger.
out_of_scope: Automated dispute decisioning using machine learning.

requirements.text: Merchants sign in and see a list of their open and closed chargebacks with amount, reason code, deadline and status.
Merchants upload evidence documents (PDF, JPG, PNG up to 20 MB each) against a chargeback before the network deadline.
The system submits the evidence package to the card network dispute API and records the submission receipt.
Chargeback notifications from the card networks are ingested and create or update dispute cases automatically.
Operations analysts work a case queue, assign cases, add internal notes and change case status.
Email notifications to merchants when a chargeback is created, 3 days before the evidence deadline, and when an outcome is received.
Analysts see a dashboard of disputes by status, reason code, win rate and deadline risk.
Merchants can accept liability for a chargeback with one click, closing the case.
Dispute outcomes (won or lost) are posted to the internal payments ledger to adjust merchant balances.
Bulk evidence upload for merchants with many disputes.
Portal pages load in under 2 seconds at p95 for 500 concurrent merchants.
99.9% monthly availability for the merchant portal.
Merchant SSO via OAuth2; analysts via corporate SSO; role-based access so merchants only see their own disputes.
Evidence documents and card data encrypted at rest and in transit; card numbers must never be stored in clear text.
Full audit trail of every case action retained for 7 years.
The system should be easy to use for merchants.
Visa and Mastercard dispute APIs (REST, certification required).
Internal payments ledger API.
Corporate email service.
Target go-live within 20 weeks of kickoff.
Team of 7 engineers available.
Must run on the org AWS platform.

stakeholders: Head of Merchant Operations (sponsor), Merchant Operations analysts, Risk and Compliance, Payments Platform team.
success_metrics: Average dispute handling time of 4 days or less within 3 months of launch.
open_questions: Do we need to support Amex disputes in phase 1?

flags.message: NFR-06 uses vague terms ['easy', 'easy to use']; acceptance criteria cannot be derived.
flags.resolution: Agents must quantify using org defaults and mark as assumption; confirm with product owner.
